question: Why does someone behind the reflecting locus fail to perceive the original?
premises: A person standing behind a mirror does not directly know the original face.
An echo involves a reflecting spatial locus analogous to a mirror.
A person standing behind such a reflecting space is similarly positioned.
inference: One behind the reflecting acoustic space does not directly know the original sound, just as one behind a mirror does not directly know the original face.
uncertainties: tathāvidhākāśa is read as a space of the same reflecting kind described in verse 31.
plain_english: Just as someone standing behind a mirror does not directly know the face, someone standing behind such a reflecting space does not directly know the original sound.
